title: Synkrisis: a browser-based tool for the comparative evaluation of translation versions
description: Synkrisis is a self-contained, browser-based tool for the comparative evaluation of translation versions (human and machine translations, retranslations) within the same language: segmentation, alignment and collation against a base text, with descriptive annotation based on an adapted subset of van Leuven-Zwart's model of translation shifts and evaluative annotation based on selected MQM error types, without scoring. Every annotation category comes with a definition. Texts are processed locally in the browser and are not stored. Includes an annotated example session (Alphonse Daudet, 'La mule du Pape', five machine translation outputs into Greek). Version 1.1.0 adds definitions for all categories, an export of annotations as a 0/1 table with stable keys, and the tool and annotation-scheme versions in the session and CSV files; categories and their keys are unchanged, and 1.0.0 sessions open without conversion. The definitions of the evaluative categories are abridged paraphrases of those in the MQM Core typology (The MQM Council, themqm.org, CC BY 4.0) and are released under the same licence. Developed by Eleni Tziafa, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens. Designed and implemented in collaboration with Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic). Live version: https://elenitziafa.com/synkrisis.html
